engines.name: Dual-motor electric e-4ORCE AWD (63 or 87 kWh)

issues.t: "Service EV System" warning and sudden shutdown
issues.sym: A "Service EV System" or "EV System Off" message appears and the car cuts to very low power or shuts down completely, sometimes at highway speed. The battery reading may suddenly drop toward 0%, and the car may not restart until it is towed and reset.
issues.why: This is the most-reported Ariya complaint to NHTSA. Causes vary: inverter and battery-management software faults (some covered by recalls on 2023 models), a weak 12-volt battery, or a fault in the high-voltage system that the dealer has to read from stored codes.
issues.next: Move to a safe spot and turn on your hazards. Have the car towed to a Nissan dealer, ask for the stored codes to be read, and make sure every recall and software update for your VIN is done. The high-voltage parts are covered by Nissan's 8-year/100,000-mile EV warranty.

issues.t: Inverter software can cut drive power (recall)
issues.sym: The car can suddenly lose drive power while you are driving, with EV system warnings on the dash.
issues.why: Software in the inverter, the unit that feeds power to the motors, can wrongly detect a short circuit and shut the drive system off. NHTSA campaign 23V-657 covers almost 10,000 Ariyas.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and book the free inverter software update with a Nissan dealer.

issues.t: Inverter error check can shut the car down (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden loss of drive power with a warning message, even though nothing is actually broken.
issues.why: A second inverter software problem lets the system misread an error and shut down the EV system. This is NHTSA campaign 24V-560, separate from the 2023 inverter recall.
issues.next: Ask a Nissan dealer to confirm the inverter software version and update it for free if needed.

issues.t: Front motor oil leak can cut power (recall)
issues.sym: Possible loss of drive power with warning lights. You probably won't see the leak, because the oil leaks inside the motor.
issues.why: O-ring seals in the front drive motor may have been damaged when it was built, so oil leaks internally and the motor can stop working (NHTSA campaign 24V-391, a small number of early cars).
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. Nissan replaces the whole front motor for free.

issues.t: Steering wheel bolt may be loose or missing (recall)
issues.sym: The steering wheel may feel loose or move on the column. In the worst case it could come off while driving.
issues.why: On some early cars, the bolt holding the steering wheel to the column was not tightened correctly or was left out (NHTSA campaign 23V-131).
issues.next: If the wheel feels loose at all, do not drive the car; have it towed to a dealer. Otherwise check your VIN and get the free bolt replacement done.

issues.t: Front motor bolts may be overtightened after recall repair
issues.sym: A clunk or other unusual noise from the front suspension area on a car that had its front motor replaced under recall.
issues.why: The repair instructions for the front motor recall gave the wrong tightening spec, so the two front motor mounting bolts may have been overtightened and can loosen later. Nissan opened free service campaign P6A01 for the affected cars.
issues.next: If your car had the front motor recall done, ask a Nissan dealer whether campaign P6A01 applies. The bolt replacement is free and takes about an hour.

issues.t: Weak 12-volt battery stops the car from powering on
issues.sym: The car won't turn on, the app can't reach it, or you get a string of warnings even though the main battery shows plenty of charge. Charging may start and stop.
issues.why: Like gas cars, the Ariya uses a small 12-volt battery to wake up its computers and connect the main battery. Some 12-volt batteries have failed early, and Nissan issued a bulletin about the 12-volt charging logic.
issues.next: Have the 12-volt battery load-tested and the DC-DC converter checked for proper charging. A young battery that fails is often replaced under warranty, and a software update may be part of the fix.

issues.t: DC fast charging stops early or won't start
issues.sym: A fast-charging session fails to start, stops after a minute or so, or the car shuts down at the charger with an "EV System Off" message.
issues.why: Communication between the car and the charger can fail. A weak 12-volt battery, a DC-DC converter fault, a damaged charge port or a particular charging network can be to blame.
issues.next: Try a different charger or network and restart the car. If it keeps happening on several networks, have the dealer check the 12-volt battery, DC-DC converter and charge port under warranty.

issues.t: Won't charge because charge port caps are missing
issues.sym: The car will not take a charge through the high-voltage charge port.
issues.why: Nissan issued a bulletin (NTB24-040) for cars where one or two terminal caps inside the charge port are missing.
issues.next: Ask a Nissan dealer to inspect the charge port against the bulletin. This should be a warranty repair.

issues.t: Screens freeze, go blank or reboot
issues.sym: The center screen or digital gauge cluster freezes, goes black or restarts. Navigation and instruments may drop out for a while, and some owners report display units changing on their own.
issues.why: Software in the infotainment unit and the CAN gateway, the module that passes messages between the car's computers, has needed updates. Nissan ran service campaigns P4A30 and P4A31 to reprogram both.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to check that the gateway and infotainment software are current. Pull over safely if the gauge cluster goes blank while driving.

issues.t: Driver-assist false alerts or ProPILOT unavailable
issues.sym: Collision warnings with nothing ahead, a "ProPILOT unavailable" message, or lane-keeping that behaves oddly, especially after windshield or front-end work.
issues.why: The radar and camera sensors must be aimed precisely. Nissan issued bulletins on side radar alignment and driver-assist fault codes.
issues.next: Keep the sensors and windshield clean. If warnings keep appearing, ask the dealer to check the codes and recalibrate the radar and camera. Always insist on recalibration after glass or bumper work.

issues.sym: The 360-degree camera view looks stitched together wrong, with lines or images that don't match up.
issues.why: The around-view cameras need calibrating. Nissan issued a bulletin (NTB23-076B) on the calibration procedure.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to recalibrate the around-view monitor, especially after a mirror, bumper or liftgate repair.
